question.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the general obligations of the Sponsor/Manager/Trustee of an AIF under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012 as described in Chapter 7?

answer.text: Compulsory appointment of a SEBI-registered custodian for safekeeping of securities.
Annual audit of books of accounts by a qualified auditor.
Maintenance of records (assets, valuation, investor details, investment decisions) for 5 years after winding up of the fund.
Mandatory appointment of a SEBI-registered investment adviser to approve every investment.

explanation.text: The Logic: The general obligations listed in Chapter 7 are: compulsory custodian appointment, policy/procedure review, annual audit, dispute-resolution mechanism, 5-year record retention post winding up, and full SEBI inspection cooperation. Mandatory appointment of a SEBI-registered Investment Adviser to clear each investment is NOT a listed obligation — offshore funds may voluntarily engage IAs but domestic AIFs typically do not. The Trap: Options A, B, C are all direct obligations listed in the chapter. D is fabricated and contradicts the practice note that 'Domestic funds do not generally have the practice of appointing investment advisors'. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (IA) tests the IA appointment separately. III-A/C Compliance tests document-retention standards. XIX-C combines it into the general-obligations framework.
